- CLAUDE.md:lines 1968–1988 (§26.D rename-and-archive paragraph) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The "Check the target first" warning is positioned AFTER the unconditional rename/archive/delete actions in the same paragraph. The text reads in linear order: (1) rename the checker to `PR #<n> <state> — handed to <this session's id>`, (2) `archives it (archive_session)`, (3) `and only then deletes the fired Routine (delete_trigger, ignoring not-found)`, (4) THEN "**Check the target first:** call `get_session` on the checker id and rename or archive it only when [title matches]". The plan's Implementation Step 2 explicitly required "before renaming or archiving the checker, get_session that id" — the intent was check-first, but the diff delivers check-last, in the same run-on paragraph as the actions it should gate.
  WHY: A fixer following the literal paragraph top-to-bottom performs the rename and archive on the wrong session before reaching the bold "Check the target first" heading. Even with the bold cue, the surrounding imperative statements lack conditional language ("only when its title is..."), so a fixer reading the actions first has nothing to tell them those actions are gated by a check they have not yet run. The exact bug this PR exists to prevent — renaming or archiving the wrong session — is reintroduced by the very paragraph that documents the fix. The test `test_fixer_checks_the_checker_before_renaming_or_archiving` only checks for phrase presence (no order assertion), so it passes despite the ordering defect. The fix is mechanical: move the "Check the target first" block (with the "otherwise skip both calls" and "Say 'archived' only after..." sentences) ahead of the rename/archive/delete sentence, so the paragraph reads "check first, then rename, then archive, then delete the routine".
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
